title: Sharabhanga
hook: an old man lights a fire and steps into it, and then the other sages show Rama what they've been hiding

segments.voice: Yesterday: Sharabhanga, part one. Indra left before Rama came, and the old sage offered Rama all his merit. Rama said: I'll earn my own worlds. Did you take one step on your own? Day five hundred fifty-six.

Sharabhanga asks Rama to wait and watch. Then he builds a fire, makes the offering of clarified butter into it, and with the words of the rite, steps into the flames. Rama, Sita and Lakshmana stand there. The old body burns away. And out of the fire, Valmiki says, rises a young man, shining, who goes up to the world of Brahma. The sage had waited only for this: to see his guest, and then to go.
screen: `WAIT AND WATCH.` → `HE STEPS INTO THE FIRE.` → `A YOUNG MAN RISES.`

segments.voice: It's important to say what this scene is and isn't. In the Ramayana, Sharabhanga is a great ascetic at the very end of a long life of tapas, who has already been invited to heaven by Indra himself. His entry into the fire is presented as a sacred departure, a completed life, not a despairing one. The text treats it with awe. Then the mood changes. Word has spread through the hermitages that Rama is here, and the sages gather around him, many kinds of ascetics, Valmiki says, some living on nothing but water, some on air, some standing in rivers. And they lead him somewhere. It's a place in the forest where bones are piled up. The bodies of sages, killed by rakshasas, the man-eating demons who roam Dandaka. Look, they say. This is what happens to us. They're slaughtering us, and we have no protector. You are our refuge. Remember what the sages asked a few days ago: be our king, protect us. Now Rama sees why. Not a vague danger, but this. And he answers them directly. I came to this forest to keep my father's word, he says, but I'll also do this. I'll destroy the rakshasas who harm you. That promise matters. It's freely made, by a man under no orders, in front of witnesses. And in the chapters ahead, it will be tested, and questioned, by someone very close to him.
screen: `A SACRED DEPARTURE, NOT DESPAIR.` · `THE SAGES GATHER.` · `A PILE OF BONES IN THE FOREST.` · `RAMA'S PROMISE.` · then, large: `I'LL PROTECT YOU.`

segments.voice: Sit and settle. Think about something you've seen recently that wasn't right: in the news, in your town, at work. Something real, not abstract. Let yourself look at it honestly for a moment, the way Rama looked at what the sages showed him. Don't flood yourself. Just look, and breathe. Then ask quietly: is there one small thing within my reach? Let the answer come, or not. The bell holds the time.
Sharabhanga. The old sage who rose from the fire to Brahma's world. After him, the sages show Rama the bones, and Rama promises to protect them.
Your line: Sharabhanga. Today, look honestly at one thing that isn't right, and do one small thing within your reach. Day five hundred fifty-six.

howItsDone: Ramayana reciters tell Sharabhanga's departure with reverence, and Rama's promise to the sages here sets up the battles later in the Aranya Kanda.

fork.setup: you're Rama. the sages show you a pile of bones and say: we have no protector. what do you do?
options: tell them to leave the forest.
promise to destroy the rakshasas who harm them.
say your exile is only to keep a promise.

original.note: Sanskrit agni: fire, and the god of fire, who carries offerings up to the gods.

trapdoor: what you thought: the sage dies in a fire.
what it means: a great ascetic completes his life, rising from the fire to Brahma's world.
what a scholar hears: Aranya 5 ends with the departure; Aranya 6 brings the bones and Rama's vow, which frames the conflicts of the forest book.
